stem: What is the primary goal of performing an epiphysiodesis on the unaffected (contralateral) limb in a patient with a limb length discrepancy?

options.text: To stimulate growth in the shorter leg through increased blood flow.
To correct an angular deformity in the fractured leg.
To stop growth in the longer leg so the shorter leg can catch up.
To prevent future articular incongruency in the joints.

explanation: By timing the closure of the growth plate in the normal, longer leg, clinicians allow the injured, shorter leg to equalize the discrepancy.
rationale: Think about how you would level two uneven objects if you could only stop the taller one from growing taller.

optionExplanations.A: Epiphysiodesis does not stimulate the opposite leg; it only stops growth in the leg being operated on.
optionExplanations.B: Epiphysiodesis is used for length correction; guided growth (like the 8-plate) is typically used for angular correction.
optionExplanations.C: By timing the closure of the growth plate in the normal, longer leg, clinicians allow the injured, shorter leg to equalize the discrepancy.
optionExplanations.D: Articular congruency is managed by anatomic reduction at the time of injury, not by leg-length procedures later.
